messages.author: 91bc9ff4be649e37
messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix error
parts:
Hi,

Hopefully this is the right place to post. I am trying to install the
"aroma.affymetrix" library on my linux (CentOS 5) machine, but I keep
getting the following error.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package 'aroma.affymetrix'
** Removing '/usr/local/bin/lib64/R/library/aroma.affymetrix'

The downloaded packages are in
/tmp/RtmpcTRzGI/downloaded_packages
Updating HTML index of packages in '.Library'
Installing/updating: BRAJU:sfit (>= 0.1.5),mac=hasBinary
Repositories: BRAJU
Package: sfit (>= 0.1.5)
Tags: mac=hasBinary
Updating packages: sfit from repository 'http://www.braju.com/R/repos'
01/01. sfit: v0.1.5, i.e. up to date.
############################################################
# #
# Packages installed/updated. Please restart R. #
# #
############################################################
Warning messages:
1: In safeSource() : Redefining ‘biocinstall’
2: In safeSource() : Redefining ‘biocinstallPkgGroups’
3: In safeSource() : Redefining ‘biocinstallRepos’
4: In install.packages(pkgs = "aroma.affymetrix", type = "source", :
installation of package 'aroma.affymetrix' had non-zero exit status

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I am new to R so I am not sure where the error is coming from if it
helps here is my session Info

R version 2.7.2 (2008-08-25)
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

Thanks.

Sincerely,
Ben

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] aroma.affymetrix error
parts:
Hi Ben.

One suggestion would be to use the latest version of R. Your version
is not that old, but R (and aroma.affymetrix) does move quickly and
the installation instructions suggest using the latest update of R.

Try that and if still no success, can you give the whole output of
your installation from a fresh R session. I assume there is more to
the installation than what is shown below.

Cheers,
Mark
